items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: Hazel Scott was the pianist. The intermission pianist there. She was about 18 or 19 years old when I played there.

ctx.x: I had played for. They made me feel good cause they came out in droves. They said I drew more than any big band out there during those years for dances. I won't say for theaters and all that, but for dances, we did draw very big through those years cause I did have records like 2 and 3 and 4 on all the vendors during that time when my records was very hot.

It's kind of hard for me to pick one highlight. I don't know cause I really enjoyed them all. You know? And what I had mentioned to you, but once I got to downtown on Broadway, oh, at the theaters. I had played Broadway like uptown, Harlem Uptown House, Harlem Uptown. That was the first club on 51st, 52nd and Broadway. Hazel Scott was the pianist. The intermission pianist there. She was about 18 or 19 years old when I played there.
And, another theater I played at was Loew's State which you could only do about 20 minutes cause they had kind of acts. You know, they did 5 or 10 minutes, but the band just did 20 minutes.
